## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

Sekhiya 61 of the *Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga*, titled *Pāduka* ("Wearing shoes"), is a monastic training rule governing the proper circumstances under which a monk may expound the Dhamma. The rule prohibits a bhikkhu from teaching the Dhamma to anyone wearing shoes or sandals unless that person is ill, as listening to the Dhamma while wearing footwear is regarded as showing disrespect [Bodhi 2003; Dhammika 2005]. The rule is occasionally discussed in contemporary literature in connection with Vinaya etiquette during modern public lectures or inter-religious meetings, where non-monastics may be requested to remove their shoes before a discourse begins [Dhammika 2005]. A modern English translation has been produced by Bhikkhu Brahmali.

Within the Pali canon, the rule corresponds directly to Sekhiya 61 in the *Bhikkhu Pātimokkha*, the *Bhikkhu Parivāra*, and the parallel nuns' rules in the *Bhikkhunī Vibhaṅga*, *Bhikkhunī Pātimokkha*, and *Bhikkhunī Parivāra*. It is also widely attested across the Vinayas of other early Buddhist schools, with extant parallels in Chinese and Sanskrit belonging to the Sarvāstivāda, Mūlasarvāstivāda, Mahīśāsaka, Mahāsāṅghika, Dharmaguptaka, Lokottaravāda, and Kāśyapīya traditions, as well as the *Upāliparipṛcchā*. DharmaNexus matches show internal Pali text reuse across 41 other Vinaya passages (94 matching units), sharing formulaic procedural framing most closely with adjacent pedagogical Sekhiya rules such as Sekhiya 64, 66, 67, and 63 [DharmaNexus].
